title: A clump of galaxy misfits
caption: Hickson Compact Group 59, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: HCG 59 · constellation Leo · about 180 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Galaxies of very different kinds share this Hubble frame. There are two large spirals, one seen face-on with smooth arms and delicate threads of dust, the other steeply tilted. Beside them is a strangely disorderly galaxy with clumps of blue young stars, and many smaller, probably more distant galaxies fill the background.

This is Hickson Compact Group 59. The astronomer Paul Hickson cataloged unusually tight groupings of galaxies in 1982, and this was the 59th in his list. The group stands out for how varied its members are.

Hickson groups tend to be peculiar places. They often give off radio and infrared light and host active star-forming regions. Their galaxies frequently contain active galactic nuclei, bright centers powered by supermassive black holes, and large amounts of dark matter, the unseen material detected only by its gravity.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.95 x 2.66 arcminutes) and distance (180 million light years), the frame spans roughly 154,000 × 139,000 light-years. Its light set out about 180 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines blue, yellow and near-infrared filters (F435W, F606W and F814W) on Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and exposures lasting most of an hour per filter reveal faint background galaxies far beyond what an eye could see.

behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture was made with the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys through blue, yellow and near-infrared filters, with total exposures of 57, 41 and 35 minutes. It covers about 3.4 arcminutes of sky.
alt: A group of galaxies, including a face-on spiral, a tilted spiral and a disorderly galaxy with blue clumps, with many small galaxies in the background.
